solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tries during proper practice session

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other

parts.note: proper means real, genuine
a judge tries a case, that is hears it

explanation.surface: Someone attempts things properly during a rehearsal-style session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts, but here it is the courtroom sense: a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through held before a performance is the standard name for a practice session.

clue.text: Swiss dish in bistro's tip-top

indicators.note: in says the dish sits inside the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A Swiss speciality served in a first-rate bistro.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss fried potato cake, a classic national dish.

clue.text: Flourishing and rich, having been given a fresh start

indicators.text: having been given a fresh start
indicators.note: a fresh start means the first letter of the synonym is swapped for a new one

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: Someone thriving and wealthy after starting their life anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flourishing is in good health and vigour, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sweetheart turned up after a spring vegetable

indicators.note: after places the turned piece behind the a-plus-spring pieces

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sugar is an endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A lover appears following the arrival of spring, among the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green spring vegetable eaten as spears.

clue.text: Large cat paws one lord ferociously

indicators.note: ferociously suggests wild thrashing, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A big cat savagely claws at a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is a large wild feline of the Himalayan mountains.

clue.text: Cheek and other facial feature

definitions.meaning: cheek here is insolence, impudent back-talk
a mouth's fleshy edge is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Two parts of the face named together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' looks like the body part, but it means insolence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip is slang for impudent talk and also the fleshy edge of the mouth.

clue.text: One after fur points to omniverous animal

indicators.note: after puts the numeral behind the fur

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A ranking of animals by fur pointing to an omnivore.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American raccoon relative that eats both plants and small animals.

clue.text: Light-hearted teasing from her, initially, in snack bar

indicators.note: in places the initial inside the snack bar word

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe or snack bar

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word her

explanation.surface: A woman joking around with friends in a snack bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A CAFF is British slang for a cheap, basic cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is good-humoured banter, joking ribbing among friends.

clue.text: Style of design poorly rated by small company

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are in bad shape and need rearranging

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A design style given a low rating by a minor firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Indecorum shown in memo I'd rewritten with pen

indicators.note: rewritten says these letters are written out again in another order

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Improper behaviour revealed in a memo redrafted with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like the writing tool, but it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, as is immodesty in behaviour or dress.

clue.text: Drive off to get hold of a representative for a cleaning preparation

indicators.note: to get hold of means the first piece wraps around the others

parts.note: shoo means drive away
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: Chasing someone away to grab an agent for a cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid preparation for washing hair or carpets.

clue.text: Husband in Christmas show, male ghost

indicators.note: in puts the husband's letter inside the show

parts.note: a panto, pantomime, is a British Christmas stage show

explanation.surface: A husband appearing in a seasonal show as a male ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is pantomime, a comic family stage show put on in Britain around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a spectre or apparition, another word for a ghost.

clue.text: Bury playwright needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright

explanation.surface: A well-known dramatist from Bury, so famous he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter someone is to lay a body in the grave, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Abandoned speciality, unconventional

parts.note: something abandoned is left behind
a person's field is their area of expertise

explanation.surface: Someone gave up their specialism to do something unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-field, from baseball, describes ideas that are odd or out of the mainstream.

clue.text: Withstanding attack very well

definitions.meaning: read literally, fit for combat and able to hold off an assault
the idiom means in peak health and condition

explanation.surface: Holding firm under assault and doing splendidly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in excellent shape, literally fit enough for a battle.

clue.text: See no odds for replay

indicators.note: no odds means the odd-numbered letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Watch a replay with no betting odds offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a bishop's see: Ely is a Cambridgeshire cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is the seat of one.

clue.text: Vehicle's condition described by retired people

indicators.note: described by means surrounded by, as a line is drawn around a figure
retired means withdrawn backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a race is a people
state means condition

explanation.surface: The state of a car as reported by pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired people' suggests pensioners, but 'retired' is the reversal signal; 'described by' means drawn around, so the condition sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Grocer goes off to collect second bravery award

indicators.note: to collect means the jumbled letters gather the extra one inside them
off says the letters go wrong and are shuffled

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper heads out to pick up a medal for courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges GROCERGOES, and 'to collect' takes in S.
explanation.definitionFit: The George Cross is a British decoration for civilian gallantry.

clue.text: Sure-fire winner in TT race crashed, sadly, at the end

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters are smashed up and reassembled
at the end picks out the final letter of the word sadly

explanation.surface: A favourite in the motorcycle TT race crashes, unhappily, at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' turns INTTRACE into CERTAINT. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty is a bet or contestant sure to win, a dead cert.

clue.text: Some tartan cloth finally used to make a cap

indicators.note: used to make says these letters are the raw material reshaped into something new
finally picks out the final letter of the word cloth

explanation.surface: Tartan material used to make a Scottish cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' is not a hidden-word signal here: its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tam-o'-shanter is a round woollen Scottish bonnet with a bobble.

clue.text: Evaluate course of action

definitions.meaning: to evaluate is to gauge or size something up
a step taken to achieve something, as in emergency steps

explanation.surface: Assess the plan you are taking.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure is to assess, and a measure is a step taken, as in safety measures.

clue.text: Last time out, for example

indicators.note: out means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: to last is to stay, endure

explanation.surface: The most recent time someone was out, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an instance, just like e.g.

clue.text: Some consult an Asian sovereign's wife

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people seek advice from an Asian ruler's consort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife of a sultan, a Muslim sovereign.

clue.text: Grade neat new restaurant

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Rating a smart new eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor place serving refreshments, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Apportion a rising levy

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: Share out an increasing tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or assign shares, a synonym.

clue.text: Improvised, most of excuse involving daughter

indicators.note: involving means taking the other letter inside
most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an alibi is an excuse

explanation.surface: Making up most of an excuse that drags in a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-lib describes speech made up on the spot, without preparation.

clue.text: Busy person starts to chop hickory wood

parts.note: busy as a bee: a bee is a byword for a hard worker

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A busy worker begins chopping hickory timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hickory wood' looks like the definition; hickory gives only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech is a hardwood timber from the beech tree.

clue.text: Pair left in car heading for Truro

indicators.note: in places the side letter inside the car

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of Truro

explanation.surface: Two people left in a car bound for Truro, a Cornish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of rhyming lines of verse.

clue.text: Dump mine on the way up

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: Discard the mine while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIP is British for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a refuse site, and to tip is also to dump a load.

clue.text: Price of ticket needed by supporter for elaborate ceremony

indicators.note: needed by puts the fare after the supporter

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
a fare is the price of a travel ticket

explanation.surface: A fan must pay the ticket price for a grand event.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanfare means showy display or ostentatious ceremony, as in launched with great fanfare.

clue.text: Butler's nasty threat following removal of article?

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged
following removal of means the word loses the given letter first

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A manservant makes a menacing threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from THREAT to get THRET, and 'nasty' rearranges it. 'Butler' is not a servant but Rhett Butler of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhett is the first name of Butler, the hero of Gone with the Wind.

clue.text: Money for minor expenses small- minded Conservative has blown

parts.note: small-minded means petty

indicators.note: blown suggests the letters are blasted apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mean Tory has squandered the office kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty cash is a small fund kept for incidental office spending.
